column1: Valuation of insurance contract liabilities (being insurance and reinsurance contract assets and liabilities) in the consolidated financial statements
See notes 2(c), 2(z), 4, 5, 6, 23 and 34 (g) to the consolidated financial statements

column2: How the matter was addressed in our audit

For the valuation of the liability for incurred claims (LIC) for PAA contracts across
the Group, we assessed management’s valuation models. We assessed the
adequacy of the assumptions applied by management e.g., claims ratio, claims
triangles, reinsurance recovery rates, and assessed the adequacy of the year-end
valuation with amongst others reference to prior years and key ratios; and
We assessed the adequacy of the insurance contract balances disclosures in the
consolidated financial statements in accordance with IFRS 17 requirements.

column1:
The Directors have prepared the consolidated and separate financial statements on
the basis of accounting applicable to a going concern.
We considered the application of the going concern basis of accounting and the
related disclosures in these financial statements to be a key audit matter due to the
following:
The cumulative losses and negative cashflows from operating activities for the
group and the company as at 31 December 2024 were material;
The group’s and the company’s significant borrowings due to mature in the year
ending 31 December 2025 and the measures put in place to resolve liquidity
challenges and raise additional funds to settle the outstanding obligations which
include significant judgements and assumptions regarding cash flows.
Due to the significant judgements made by the Directors in their evaluation of the
group’s and the company’s ability to continue as a going concern, we considered this
to be a key audit matter.
column2:
Our audit procedures in this area included:
evaluation of the Directors’ assessment of the group’s and the company’s going
concern for at least the next 12 months from the approval of these financial
statements by:
• examining the group’s and the company’s financial forecasts and understanding
the underlying assumptions that the directors have used in preparing these
forecasts. This involved evaluating the reasonableness of these forecasts
based on evidence provided to support the underlying assumptions;
• comparing the actual performance for the year ended 31 December 2024 to the
budget and prior year in order to determine the reasonableness of the budgets
and the historical accuracy of management forecasts;
• understanding the debt restructuring agreements with existing lenders through
reading of correspondence between the Directors, the Insurance Regulatory
Authority (IRA) and the existing lenders;
evaluation of the adequacy of the disclosures made in the consolidated and
separate financial statements in respect of judgements and plans made with
respect to going concern assessment.
